article_title: Docker Ships Fixed Hardened Images for Java4Shell on Three Runtimes, Patches Two NGINX HTTP/2 Flaws

content_preview.title: Docker Ships Fixed Hardened Images for Java4Shell on Three Runtimes, Patches Two NGINX HTTP/2 Flaws
content_preview.summary: Docker's Hardened Images catalog now carries fixed builds for the Java4Shell flaw on three OpenJDK runtimes and for two NGINX HTTP/2 bugs, while Eclipse Temurin remains unpatched.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Docker has started shipping rebuilt Docker Hardened Images that fix the "Java4Shell" Java runtime flaw and two unrelated NGINX HTTP/2 vulnerabilities, according to a [Docker blog post](https://www.docker.com/blog/docker-patches-java4shell-and-the-nginx-http-2-with-docker-hardened-images/). The update, posted November 19, closes a gap left open by the vulnerability's initial disclosure two days earlier: which downstream Java builds had actually shipped a fix. As [previously reported]...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean News-format follow-up (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Why It Matters), 797 words, within the 400-1200 News range. Dense with specific version strings and CVE/version-range detail, all correctly hedged as Docker's or nginx.org's own account rather than the Herald's independent findings.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both manifest snapshots verified by sha256 (source-0.html.gz = c086e153eab216a2cf4c53a777dd24e6a3cb304ccd56f75cc4f7ef71a44fdeec matches manifest; source-1.html.gz = fa0e7636a9c4d97d27b6c3862ab5176e7f7a6b4511451038ed6f19584e79b009 matches manifest); no suspicious_patterns flagged on either. Read full decompressed text of both. Source 1 (docker.com blog, 'Docker patches Java4Shell and the NGINX HTTP/2 with Docker Hardened Images', posted Nov 19 2026): confirms disclosure dates (Java4Shell Nov 17, NGINX fixes 'the next day' = Nov 18), DHI publishing fixed images 'starting that same day' (Nov 18), the memory-corruption/Base64-decoder root-cause description, the AVX-512 VBMI hardware gating, the pre-auth/post-auth target lists (Keycloak/Jira/Confluence/Artifactory/Jenkins/PingFederate pre-auth; Kafka/Solr/Elasticsearch/Gerrit/Spinnaker post-auth), the 'no universal exploit' quote, 'no public reports of exploitation' as of Nov 18, the per-runtime patch table (Corretto 17.0.21.1.2/27.0.1.1.4, SapMachine 21.0.13.1+2, Zulu 17.0.21.1+2, Temurin still unfixed with only the x86-64 Linux 27.0.1.1+4 build out and three lines - 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1 - still in testing), the -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics mitigation, the Java 26 EOL/no-fix line, the NGINX CVE numbers, the NGINX 1.30.7/1.31.9 rebuild dates, and the Calif AI-cost quote ('used AI to find this flaw in about an hour and that the whole effort cost less than $200 in tokens'). Source 2 (nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html): independently confirms CVE-2026-123007 = 'Memory corruption in HTTP/2 flow control', severity 'major', vulnerable 1.9.5-1.31.8, not vulnerable 1.31.9+/1.30.7+; and CVE-2026-123633 = 'Use-after-free in HTTP/2', severity 'medium', vulnerable 1.19.7-1.31.8, not vulnerable 1.31.9+/1.30.7+. Both CVE numbers, titles, severities and version ranges in the article match the nginx.org table exactly. Anthropic disclosure: not required - Anthropic/Claude is not the subject of this story and is not mentioned.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Quote-by-quote audit of every double-quoted string in body_markdown against the Docker snapshot: (1) 'a memory-corruption bug in the Java runtime that can let an attacker with no credentials run code inside a Java application' - verbatim match. (2) 'miscalculates a length when the input ends in unexpected padding and writes up to 62 bytes past the end of a buffer on the Java heap' - verbatim match. (3) 'note there is no universal exploit: each application needs its own, and they have not published those' - verbatim match. (4) 'says it used AI to find this flaw in about an hour and that the whole effort cost less than $200 in tokens' - verbatim match. No hallucinated or paraphrased-as-verbatim quotes found. Non-quoted paraphrases (pre/post-auth target lists, patch-table version strings, NGINX CVE descriptions, mitigation flag, Java 26 EOL) all check out against the source text. Ran the policy quantifier/absence scan (no/none/only/every/each/all/never/first/last/any) over title+summary+body: every flagged sentence traces to an explicit Docker or nginx.org statement and is correctly attributed ('Docker says', 'according to Docker') rather than asserted as the Herald's own finding - e.g. the 'no public reports of exploitation' absence claim is Docker's account, not independently verified by the Herald, and is phrased that way. Headline, summary and lead are each backed by the Docker source; no orphan body URL (both sources.length appear in body and vice versa, confirmed by the automated body_sources_match/sources_referenced checks).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and technical throughout; no sensationalism, no AI self-reference, hedged attribution used consistently ('Docker says', 'according to Docker', 'Docker's post adds').
editor_notes.originality: Genuine follow-up, not a duplicate. The Herald's existing Nov 18 article (src/content/articles/2026-11/18-java4shell-...) explicitly left open in its 'What We Don't Know' section: 'it is also not clear from the sources reviewed which specific downstream JVM builds - such as Eclipse Temurin, Microsoft Build of OpenJDK, and Azul Zulu - have already shipped their own patched releases.' This submission directly answers that open question with Docker's runtime-by-runtime patch table, and adds wholly new, unrelated material (the two NGINX HTTP/2 CVEs) not touched by the Nov 18 article. Checked all of src/content/articles/2026-11/ for NGINX or Docker-Hardened-Images coverage: no article mentions nginx, and the one 'hardened images' grep hit (13-apache-http-server-2471...) is an unrelated mod_http2 story. No overlap found.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Well-sourced, accurate follow-up to the Herald's own Nov 18 Java4Shell coverage that closes a gap that article explicitly flagged as unknown, plus genuinely new NGINX HTTP/2 vulnerability coverage. Every direct quote verified verbatim against the Docker snapshot; both NGINX CVE numbers, severities and version ranges independently verified against nginx.org and matched exactly. No fabrications, no misattribution, no orphan sources. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, concrete operational follow-up (a patch-status table across JVM vendors) useful to a defined security/ops audience, not a broad-audience or industry-changing story.
